text: Agents are created once and can be resumed later from any device, session, or interface, keeping their identity and memory intact.
quote: create an agent once, then resume it from anywhere. Each agent has its own identity and long-term memory

text: Provides a self-hosted App Server to run local agents on a central always-on machine and expose them via the Agent SDK.
quote: Run the Letta App Server to host local agents on a central, always-on machine and expose them to client applications

text: Agents can run entirely on infrastructure you control, i.e. the product is fully self-hostable.
quote: Letta agents can run entirely on infrastructure you control

text: 'Dreaming' runs background subagents that review conversations and consolidate lessons into memory, with configurable triggers.
quote: Dreaming uses background subagents to review recent conversations, consolidate useful lessons, and update memory without interrupting your active work.

text: Headless mode lets the CLI run non-interactively for scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and UNIX tool composition.
quote: Headless mode allows you to run Letta Code non-interactively, making it easy to integrate into scripts, CI/CD pipelines, or compose with other UNIX tools.

text: /fork branches the current conversation, including its in-context history, without altering the original thread.
quote: Use /fork to branch the current conversation, including its in-context history. The new conversation can take a different direction without changing the original thread

text: /remember lets you explicitly teach the agent a lesson; the agent decides where it belongs and commits the update to memory.
quote: You can also teach it explicitly with `/remember`: `> /remember always use pnpm in this repo`. The agent decides where the lesson belongs and commits the update to MemFS.

text: Shared memory repositories, backed by Git in Letta Cloud, give multiple agents access to the same files and working context.
quote: Shared memory gives multiple agents access to the same files and working context. Each shared memory repository is a Git repository hosted in Letta Cloud

text: A local mode keeps all agent state (messages, memory, provider connections) on-device with no cloud account required.
quote: all agent state, including messages, memory, and provider connections, stays on-device, and no Letta account is required.

text: A MemFS Search mod adds keyword search plus optional semantic or hybrid search over agent memory.
quote: For keyword search and optional semantic or hybrid search, install the MemFS Search mod

text: Free/base plans cap agents at 20, while a developer plan allows unlimited agents with usage-based pricing.
quote: With a developer plan, you can create an unlimited number of agents but pay usage-based pricing.

text: A free tier is available by bringing your own API keys or coding plans (ChatGPT/Codex, Kimi, Z.AI) instead of paying Letta directly.
quote: You can get started with Letta for free by using models with BYOK, including coding plans from ChatGPT/Codex, Kimi, and Z.AI.

text: Official Letta Agent SDK for building agents into TypeScript/JavaScript applications.
quote: the Letta Agent SDK for building agents into TypeScript applications

text: SDK's createAgent() creates a stateful agent and returns an ID used to open sessions and manage it later.
quote: Create a stateful agent with `client.createAgent()`. It returns the agent's ID as a string, which you use to open sessions and manage the agent later.

text: SDK streaming returns typed events for an entire turn — reasoning, assistant text, tool calls, and tool results.
quote: The stream yields typed events for the whole turn — reasoning, assistant text, tool calls, tool results — and terminates after the turn's `result` message

text: SDK's resumeSession() can resume either an agent's default conversation or a specific conversation by ID.
quote: `resumeSession(id)` accepts either kind of ID: pass an `agent-xxx` ID to resume the agent's default conversation, or a `conv-xxx` ID to resume a specific conversation.

text: SDK supports connecting MCP servers over local stdio, Streamable HTTP, and legacy SSE transports.
quote: The SDK supports local stdio processes, Streamable HTTP, and legacy SSE

text: MCP tools are discovered from servers configured via mcpServers and proxied to them by the SDK host.
quote: MCP tools are discovered from servers supplied through `mcpServers` and proxied by the SDK host to the MCP server.

text: Agent SDK can expose custom tools directly from your own Node.js process.
quote: The Agent SDK can expose two kinds of tools through your Node.js process

text: The App Server exposes an OpenAI-compatible API usable with clients like Open WebUI.
quote: use the App Server’s OpenAI-compatible API with clients such as Open WebUI, or the ACP adapter with ACP clients such as Zed

text: letta-acp exposes a stateful agent through the Agent Client Protocol so ACP-compatible clients (e.g. Zed) can drive it.
quote: `letta-acp` exposes a stateful Letta agent through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), so any ACP-compatible client can drive it.

text: With a GitHub org connected, agents on cloud computers can clone/read/push repos to sweep bug reports, open PRs, or explore code.
quote: agents running on cloud computers can access your repositories to do work — sweeping bug reports, opening pull requests, or exploring your codebase.

text: Secrets let an agent use sensitive values like API keys in shell commands without ever exposing the actual values.
quote: Secrets let your agent use sensitive values like API keys and tokens in shell commands without ever seeing the actual values.

text: Scheduled tasks let you automate prompts to an agent on a recurring schedule or at a specific future time.
quote: Scheduled tasks allow you to automate prompts to your agent on a recurring schedule or at a specific time in the future.

text: Slack integration lets agents respond always-on when mentioned in a channel or thread, using their cloud computer to do real work.
quote: Agents connected to Slack are always-on: mention them in a channel or thread and they'll respond

text: Mods let an agent modify its own runtime by adding tools, commands, event hooks, permission policies, and provider adapters live.
quote: Mods run as fully trusted code inside your Letta Code process. They let your agent modify its own runtime — adding tools, commands, event hooks, permission policies, and provider adapters

text: Skills are reusable directories of instructions/resources an agent can load when relevant, portable across Letta and other agent tools.
quote: Skills are directories containing instructions and resources that your agent can load when relevant. Think of them as reusable capability packages for specialized tasks

text: Teleportation moves an active conversation to a different computer while preserving memory and message history.
quote: Teleportation moves an active conversation to a different computer. The agent keeps its memory and message history, and continues the task on the new computer.

text: Remote environments separate where you interact with an agent from where its tools actually execute.
quote: Remote environments separate where you interact with a Letta agent from where its tools execute.

text: Teams can share agents with configurable access permissions, combining org roles with sharing controls so activity isn't visible org-wide by default.
quote: Letta combines organization roles with sharing controls so teammates can collaborate without making all agent activity visible to the entire organization.

text: Main agents can delegate to specialized subagents to handle complex tasks autonomously, keeping context clean and enabling parallelism.
quote: By delegating work to focused subagents, your main agent can keep its context window clean and make use of parallelism to divide and conquer tasks.

text: Agents are model-agnostic — you can use Claude, GPT, Gemini, or other models and switch the underlying model even mid-conversation.
quote: Letta agents are **model-agnostic**. Agents can use Claude, GPT, Gemini, or other supported models. Users can change an agent's underlying model at any time, even mid-conversation.

text: /doctor audits the memory hierarchy for misplaced content, duplication, and system-prompt token usage.
quote: If the memory hierarchy has drifted or grown too large, run /doctor to audit placement, duplication, and system-prompt token usage.

text: /init bootstraps or refreshes project memory by inspecting the repository and asking about your working style.
quote: Run `/init` to bootstrap or refresh memory for the current project. The agent inspects the repository, asks about your working style when needed

text: Desktop app and CLI can reuse your existing API keys/coding plans, while the web app runs agents in a managed cloud sandbox with no local setup.
quote: The desktop app and CLI can use your existing API keys and coding plans, while the web app runs agents in a cloud sandbox with no local setup.

text: You can connect your own machine (laptop, workstation, or cloud VM) so the agent can access its files and tools directly.
quote: To give your agent access to files and tools on your laptop, workstation, or cloud VM, connect your own machine and select it from the environment picker

text: --ephemeral runs a one-shot task without creating or persisting an agent, memory blocks, or MemFS.
quote: Use --ephemeral to run a one-shot task without creating, resuming, or persisting an agent, memory blocks, or MemFS

text: The CLI is controlled via slash commands during interactive sessions.
quote: Control Letta Code's behavior during an interactive session with slash commands.

text: CLI /agents command lets you browse and switch between agents, and /pin favorites one for quick access.
quote: Use `/agents` in the CLI to browse and switch agents. Pin an agent with `/pin` or the favorite control in the desktop app so it is easier to find later.

text: Combining Slack integration with scheduled tasks lets you create always-on digital coworkers that keep working while your laptop is closed.
quote: Agents can still be messaged even if your laptop is closed, since they have their own computer to run on. Combining agents with Slack and schedules allows you to create always-on digital coworkers.

text: Logging in backs up agents to the cloud, making them reachable via chat.letta.com, desktop app, remote machines, and messaging integrations.
quote: Run /login to back up your agents to the cloud and make them available through chat.letta.com, the desktop app, remote machines, and messaging integrations.

text: A canUseTool callback lets an app approve, deny, or edit individual tool calls interactively, e.g. with a human in the loop.
quote: a **`canUseTool` callback** that approves, denies, or edits individual tool calls — interactively, if your application involves a human.

text: A demo mobile client wires the Agent SDK to a full chat UI with streaming, tool approvals, interruption, and reconnect handling.
quote: study a mobile interface with conversation history, streaming, tools, approvals, interruption, queued messages, image attachments, and reconnect handling already wired to the portable Agent SDK

text: Passing a memory parameter gives full control over an agent's starting memory, with each entry becoming a Markdown file in its memory repository.
quote: Pass memory for full control over the agent’s starting memory. Each entry becomes a Markdown file in the agent’s memory repository

text: You can sync a GitHub organization to Letta from the Integrations page so agents can work against its repositories.
quote: Sync your GitHub org to Letta on the [Integrations] page.
